Area and economic statistics

Checked 8 October 2026. Each region shows the latest annual value found in the sources included here, with a separate year and source for each metric. Coverage is incomplete: a missing figure means it has not been verified for this dataset, not that the region has no economic activity.

Coverage

MapRegionsReported areaApprox. mapped areaGDP / real outputGDP per capita

Statistical coverage varies by country and administrative level. The dataset also includes the additional districts already present on the China map. Korea includes both South and North Korea.

Area, in km²

Reported area comes from Wikidata entity records and the published Mongolia province table. These figures can have different reference dates and definitions, including land area or total administrative area. A source without a stated date is labeled accordingly.

Where no unambiguous reported area was found, “Mapped area ≈” is calculated from the atlas’s displayed boundary polygons, with interior holes subtracted. This is approximate geometry, not an official land-area measurement. Coastlines, offshore waters, disputed boundaries and later administrative changes can cause differences. No area values are shown in square miles.

GDP and GDP per capita

GDP means nominal gross domestic product or gross regional domestic product at current prices. It is the output of the entire administrative region, not household income, wages, or the urban core alone. GDP per capita uses a published value where available. Japan’s figures are calculated from GDP and the matching-year population in the Cabinet Office prefectural accounts, with that calculation labeled; the newer census population is not used as the denominator.

China’s provincial and prefectural data use Wikipedia compilations of statistical releases, supplemented by dated regional article entries. These are secondary sources and have not all been independently audited against their original government releases. Provincial data are generally 2025 preliminary figures; many prefectural figures remain older. Undated GDP entries are excluded. Matching uses both region and province to distinguish names such as Suzhou, Fuzhou and Yulin.

South Korea’s first-level figures come from the official 2024 preliminary regional-income report, preserving its rounding. Jeonnam–Gwangju shows the sum of the two predecessor regions’ 2024 GDP, explicitly labeled; no combined GDP-per-capita estimate is supplied. A verified second-level GDP series has not yet been included.

Mongolia’s first-level figures come directly from the National Statistics Office’s regional GDP and GDP-per-capita tables, with 2025 values available for all 21 aimags and Ulaanbaatar. Soum GDP and North Korean regional GDP remain unavailable in this dataset. They are not estimated from provincial totals or population shares.

Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan use their own statistical agencies and currencies. Their districts, counties and cities do not inherit the parent region’s GDP. Taiwan’s total GDP and per-capita GDP currently come from different 2026 releases of 2025 figures; this is noted beside the source.

Japan

All 47 prefectures are included. Population uses the 2025 preliminary census as compiled in Wikipedia. GDP uses the Cabinet Office fiscal 2023 release for 42 prefectures, with fiscal 2022 values retained for the remaining five. GDP per capita is calculated using the same-year population series in the Cabinet Office accounts; it is not prefectural income per person. USD conversions use the matching calendar-year average rate. Area values are reported figures from the prefecture table; differing territorial definitions may affect comparisons with mapped boundaries.

Indonesia and the Philippines

All 38 Indonesian provinces and all 82 Philippine provinces have population, reported land area, nominal GDP and published GDP per capita. Metro Manila also displays official National Capital Region totals, including its cities and Pateros, even though it has no provinces. These cover the whole NCR, not the City of Manila alone. Country statistics load only when a supported division is selected. Cities, regencies and Philippine regions do not inherit provincial totals.

Indonesia uses BPS Statistical Yearbook 2026: 2026 midyear population projections based on the 2020 census and official 2025 provincial areas from the Ministry of Home Affairs. Projection counts are rounded to the nearest 100 people in the published table. GDP and GDP per capita use the April 2026 BPS provincial accounts, appendices 1 and 121, with 2025 very preliminary figures. Per-capita GDP uses the economic table’s 2025 population denominator.

The Philippines uses PSA OpenSTAT: 2024 census population as of 1 July 2024, land area based on the LMB/DENR 2019 masterlist, and 2025 provincial GDP and GDP per capita at current prices. Statistical province totals exclude separately reported cities even where atlas geometry includes them. Basilan figures exclude Isabela City, which is reported separately under Region IX. Maguindanao del Norte and del Sur have separate records.

Download Indonesia statistics or Philippine statistics, including source metadata.

Argentina

All 23 provinces and Buenos Aires autonomous city have population, reported area and economic-output data. The INDEC 2022–2040 projection release supplies 1 July 2026 population estimates based on the 2022 census. These are projections, not new census counts. Reported areas use IGN’s 2022 geodetic report, Table 12. Tierra del Fuego uses the 20,698.3 km² continental Americas sector displayed by the map; Antarctic and disputed South Atlantic claims are excluded from its area.

Nominal provincial GDP (PBG) and GDP per capita are verified for Buenos Aires City, Buenos Aires Province, Corrientes, Entre Ríos, Jujuy, Santa Fe, Tierra del Fuego and Tucumán. Santa Fe uses 2025 preliminary accounts; the others use 2024 provisional or preliminary accounts. Values come directly from the provincial statistics agencies. Buenos Aires Province’s total adds the 16 industry categories and net product taxes in its official table. Basic-price accounts exclude net product taxes; market-price accounts include them. Each panel identifies its valuation basis. Per-capita values divide PBG by the matching-year INDEC population unless the provincial agency publishes its own value (Santa Fe). They are not household incomes.

Every jurisdiction also has CEPAL’s March 2026 release of 2024 real gross value added at basic prices in constant 2004 pesos. This is a harmonized estimate of inflation-adjusted output, not current-price GDP, and does not replace provincial accounts. Its per-capita value uses 2024 INDEC population. Constant-price output has no current USD conversion: converting it using a 2024 exchange rate would mix incompatible price bases. Missing nominal GDP remains explicitly unavailable. Nominal USD amounts use the same-year World Bank official annual average rate, which can differ substantially from Argentina’s parallel-market rates.

Statistics load only after selecting a province or Buenos Aires City. Department, partido, comuna and city statistics are not yet included; these places do not inherit provincial totals. Download Argentina statistics and sources.

Malaysia

All 13 states and three federal territories display DOSM 2026 midyear population estimates, official 2024 land areas from Statistics Yearbook 2024, table 1.1, and DOSM 2025 real GDP at constant 2015 prices. Real GDP per capita divides this GDP by DOSM’s population for the same 2025 year. Both GDP and GDP per capita show approximate USD values in constant 2015 dollars, using the World Bank / IMF 2015 average exchange rate of 3.90550026302768 MYR per USD. The dollar estimates retain 2015 prices; they are not nominal GDP in current dollars. The July 2026 release and CSV provide a separate Putrajaya series; the catalogue still contains an older caveat about combining Putrajaya with Kuala Lumpur. The current release is used here. Population totals include non-citizens and are published in thousands, rounded to 100 people. Districts do not inherit state totals. Download Malaysia statistics and sources.

Local currency and USD

Economic figures are shown in local currency, with USD estimates where a suitable conversion is available. Nominal GDP conversions use the World Bank / IMF IFS annual average exchange-rate series for the same year as that metric. Malaysia’s real GDP instead uses the 2015 base-year rate to preserve constant prices, following the reference-year conversion method. This is a market-rate conversion, not purchasing-power parity (PPP), and may differ from the central-parity rate used in some Chinese summary tables. Taiwan’s USD figures are quoted directly from DGBAS. Exact rates and sources can be expanded in the region panel.
